title: PK Document Tracking System — Process Flow

pages.title: Sign in and find a document
pages.summary: A staff member signs in, finds an allowed record and uses its available actions.

steps.text: Sign in with the account supplied by the account administrator.
If asked, choose a new password before opening the workspace.
Open Overview, Hardcopy Documents, Softcopy Documents or External Documents.
Use folders, Search and filters; open View Details to check the full record.
Show records and actions allowed by the staff member's account permissions.
For an allowed current file, choose Download or Print when available; External Documents offer Download.

notes: Seeing a document title does not by itself allow editing, approval, download or printing.
Hardcopy records track physical documents. Softcopy and External Documents can include controlled files.

pages.title: Register or update a physical document
pages.summary: An authorized document holder records a hardcopy directly. Saving changes the live record immediately.

steps.text: Open Hardcopy Documents and choose Add New Hardcopy Document, or Edit an active record.
Enter Document Title and choose Area, Specific, optional Asset and Location.
Check Current Holder and retention dates; enter optional Reason / Notes when registering a new document.
Choose Save Document and confirm the change.
Check the active storage path, holder and dates; save the active document and its history.

notes: Only the current holder with direct hardcopy permission, or an Administrator, can edit an active hardcopy.
Administrators may select another active holder. Other users are recorded as their own holder.
Hardcopy creation and updates use this direct process. New Hardcopy Create and Update requests are unavailable.

pages.title: Monitor hardcopy storage and retention
pages.summary: The holder checks physical storage and retention dates, then chooses any required follow-up action.

steps.text: Open Hardcopy Documents and use folders or Search to find the physical document.
Open View Details and check its Area, Specific, Asset, Location and Current Holder.
When editing, enable Track retention period and enter Retention Start and Retention End.
Show the remaining days, Due today or an overdue message using office dates.
Use Due Today, Overdue, Due in the Next 7 Days or Due in 8-30 Days to review records.
Arrange a permitted update, transfer or disposal after reviewing the physical document.

notes: Both retention dates are required when tracking is enabled. Retention End must be on or after Retention Start.
Retention reminders cover allowed active hardcopies whose end date has arrived. Retention never disposes of documents automatically.
Several hardcopy documents may share one Location. The displayed Location sequence belongs to that storage place.

pages.title: Create or revise a softcopy directly
pages.summary: An authorized document controller publishes a new softcopy or replacement file without an approval request.

steps.text: Open Softcopy Documents; choose Add New Softcopy Document, or Edit a permitted active record.
Choose Create Softcopy or Revise Softcopy; enter Subject / Reason and Proposed Document Title.
For creation, choose Category; for revision, choose Existing Softcopy Document.
Check Number of Pages; attach Document File and enter optional Effective Date and Remarks.
Choose Approve Directly and confirm.
Create the active document or publish its next revision; make the approved replacement file current.

notes: The system generates a new document number. Need Series Number? allows an existing category number with a unique series.
A file is required: PDF, TXT, PNG, JPG/JPEG, DOCX or XLSX, up to 15 MB. A blank direct Effective Date uses the approval date.
Revision preserves the document number, series and category. Softcopy cancellation is unavailable; authorized disposal is separate.

pages.title: Create or revise an external document directly
pages.summary: An authorized document controller records a document received from outside the company and keeps its latest file.

steps.text: Open External Documents and choose Add New External Document, or Edit a permitted active record.
Enter Document Title, choose Category and add an optional Description.
Choose Attach File; editing also requires a replacement attachment.
Choose Save Directly and confirm.
Save an active document at revision 00, or publish the next revision and its replacement file.

notes: External Documents use External Categories and do not use retention dates.
Attach PDF, TXT, PNG, JPG/JPEG, DOCX or XLSX, up to 15 MB. Description may contain up to 2,000 characters.
Viewing a record does not automatically allow its revision or file use. Those actions need the appropriate permission and access.

pages.title: Request a softcopy or external document change
pages.summary: A requester prepares a proposed creation or revision. The live document changes only after final approval.

steps.text: Open My Requests; choose Softcopy Request or External Document Request, then New Request.
Choose Create or Revise for the selected document type and enter Subject / Reason.
For a revision, choose the existing document; enter its proposed title and other displayed details.
Choose the creation category or External Category; attach the required file and add optional Remarks.
Choose Save Draft, confirm, review the draft, then choose Submit and confirm.
Send the proposal through its published approval route; apply creation or revision after final approval.

notes: Softcopy creation also asks for Number of Pages and supports optional series. Its number and revision are assigned when approved.
External requests use External Create Request or External Revised Request; include the proposed Description and required Attach File.
Uploads accept PDF, TXT, PNG, JPG/JPEG, DOCX or XLSX, up to 15 MB. A pending attachment is not the current approved file.

pages.title: Save, submit or remove your draft
pages.summary: A requester reviews a saved proposal before submitting it, and can cancel an unsubmitted draft.

steps.text: Choose New Request in the appropriate My Requests tab and complete the displayed form.
Choose Save Draft and confirm; use Edit to correct your Draft or Returned request.
Open View Details, check the proposal and use Review File when available.
Choose Submit and confirm when the request is ready for approval.
Check permissions, active choices and required files; mark Submitted and notify the first approver.
To stop an unsubmitted draft, choose Cancel; use Delete only when offered for an eligible Cancelled draft.

notes: Only the requester can edit their Draft or Returned proposal. Submitted requests keep the approval route captured at submission.
An existing Submitted Access, Assignment or Transfer request blocks another of these for the same requester and document.
Cancel applies to Drafts. Delete permanently removes only eligible Cancelled drafts that have never entered an approval route.

pages.title: Review, approve, return or reject
pages.summary: Each assigned approver decides in order. The final approval applies the requested change or prepares a transfer.

steps.text: Open My Tasks, select the request tab and review View Details and the Approval Process Timeline.
Use Review File when offered; choose Approve, Return or Reject and confirm the decision.
Approve sends the request to the next approver; final approval applies the change.
Return sends work to the preceding approver, or to the requester when returned from the first step.
Review the return remarks; correct and resubmit the proposal, or decide the reopened approval step.
Keep the decision history. Mark a rejected request Rejected and end its approval route.

notes: Only the active step's assigned person or matching role member can decide; an administrator does not bypass that assignment.
Return and Reject allow optional remarks. Resubmission keeps the original approval route and earlier decision history.
Most final approvals mark Completed. A transfer remains Approved until its physical Dispatch and Accept steps finish.

pages.title: Request and approve a physical transfer
pages.summary: A requester proposes the receiving person and new storage place before the physical document is released.

steps.text: Open My Requests > Hardcopy Transfer Request and choose New Request.
Choose Hardcopy Document; check Original Places and Holder loaded from its current record.
Choose Destination Area, Specific, optional Asset and a different Location.
Choose Receiving User; enter Request Subject and optional Remarks, then Save Draft and Submit.
Review and approve the proposed transfer through the request's approval route.
Create a For Transfer handoff; keep the existing holder and storage place until receipt is accepted.

notes: Source and destination choices must be active and allowed. The destination needs Area, Specific and Location; Asset is optional.
The transfer requester may differ from the Current Holder. Only that original requester can later choose Dispatch.
The initial transfer route is Plant Manager, Document Control Officer, then requester confirmation. Check the published route for changes.

pages.title: Dispatch and accept the physical document
pages.summary: The original requester releases the approved hardcopy. The named recipient confirms receipt and becomes its holder.

steps.text: Open My Tasks > Hardcopy Transfer Request and find Physical Transfer Handoffs.
For a For Transfer handoff, release the physical document, choose Dispatch and confirm.
Mark the handoff In Transit and record who dispatched it and when.
After physical receipt, open the same handoff area, choose Accept and confirm.
Check the active document and Location, unchanged holder and approved storage path.
Set the receiver as holder, move the storage place, mark Accepted and complete the request.

notes: Only the original requester can Dispatch. Only the named receiving user can Accept an In Transit handoff.
Changed custody, an unavailable Location or changed approved parent places blocks acceptance and leaves the handoff unchanged.
When the holder changes, acceptance revokes the previous holder's personal hardcopy access grants. Global permissions still apply.

pages.title: Request temporary document access
pages.summary: A requester asks for time-limited access to a softcopy or hardcopy without changing its holder or assignment.

steps.text: Open My Requests > Document Access Request and choose New Request.
Choose Softcopy or Hardcopy and the document; check your name under Recipient / Assigned User.
Enter Subject / Reason, set Access Expires At after today and add optional Remarks.
Choose Save Draft, then Submit; confirm each action.
Review the access request and complete its approval route.
Grant access through the approved expiry date; keep the document's holder and assignments unchanged.

notes: Access requests are for the requester. The recipient cannot be changed to another person in this self-service form.
Expiry must still be valid at final approval. Access ends at the end of the selected date, or earlier if revoked.
An access grant still works with account permissions. Seeing a catalog record alone does not grant download, print or edit rights.

pages.title: Request a document assignment
pages.summary: A requester asks to be assigned an active softcopy or to become the holder of an active hardcopy.

steps.text: Open My Requests > Document Assignment Request and choose New Request.
Choose Softcopy or Hardcopy, select its document and check your fixed Recipient / Assigned User name.
Enter Subject / Reason and optional Remarks; choose Save Draft, then Submit and confirm.
Review the proposed assignment and complete the request's approval route.
For a softcopy, add the requester as an assignee while keeping existing assignees.
For a hardcopy, make the requester its Current Holder without changing the storage place.

notes: This request is for the requester. An authorized document controller uses Document Assignments to assign another person.
Hardcopy assignment changes custody immediately after final approval. It does not use Dispatch or Accept.
Assignment does not create a temporary access grant. The account's document and file permissions still apply.

pages.title: Assign one document or a whole storage group
pages.summary: An authorized document controller assigns a person directly, either to one document or to an entire allowed group.

steps.text: Open Document Assignments; choose Hardcopy / Places or Softcopy / Categories.
For one record, choose Assign Document, select the document and Assigned User, then Save Assignment.
For hardcopy bulk assignment, choose Location and Assigned User, then Assign All.
For softcopy bulk assignment, choose Category / Subcategory and Assigned User, then Assign All.
Check the active documents and user, the bulk limit and any active hardcopy handoffs.
Apply the whole assignment: replace hardcopy holders or add softcopy assignees; keep storage places.

notes: The required direct assignment permission is separate from permission to request an assignment.
Bulk assignment covers all active records at the Location or in the category and its subcategories, up to 2,000 records.
For Transfer or In Transit handoffs block direct hardcopy reassignment. This direct process does not use Dispatch or Accept.

pages.title: Dispose of a document directly or by request
pages.summary: An authorized person records a disposal method. A request waits for approval; a permitted direct action applies immediately.

steps.text: For a permitted direct action, open the document register and choose Dispose on an active record.
For approval, open My Requests > Disposal Request, choose New Request, then Hardcopy or External.
Choose the document and Shred, Scratch or Other; describe Other and complete the displayed request details.
Confirm direct disposal, or Save Draft and Submit the disposal request.
For a request, review the disposal and complete its approval route.
Mark the document Disposed and record the disposal method, responsible person and history.

notes: Direct disposal needs both the document's direct permission and direct disposal permission. Other needs a description of up to 250 characters.
Approved hardcopy disposal requests clear Location and revoke access grants. Direct hardcopy disposal retains those records.
Softcopy disposal is direct only and retires its controlled files. Retention dates never trigger automatic disposal.

pages.title: Maintain places and document categories
pages.summary: An authorized maintainer prepares active storage places and categories used by document forms.

steps.text: Open Setup Places and choose Area, Specific, Asset Number, Location, Softcopy Category or External Category.
Create Area first, link Specific to Area, and add optional Asset Numbers under Specific.
For Location, enter Location Name, Area and Specific; choose optional Asset Number and Archive Date.
For categories, enter the name and folder name; choose an optional parent and the softcopy code pattern.
Save and confirm; use Edit or Deactivate when permitted.
Check matching parents, category nesting and unique sequence or code rules; update future choices.

notes: A Location can omit Asset Number. Its Sequence is unique within its Specific and is assigned automatically when left empty.
Softcopy Categories and External Categories are separate. Only softcopy categories define a document numbering pattern.
Deactivation removes a choice from active selection; it does not delete the existing document records.

pages.title: Manage users, roles and permissions
pages.summary: An account administrator prepares staff accounts and limits what each role can see and do.

steps.text: Open Roles & Permissions; choose Add Role or Edit, select its allowed actions, then Save Role.
Open User Management; choose Add User or Edit and enter the staff member's account details.
Choose Primary role, Assigned roles and an optional Leader; check Active account and choose Save User.
Give the temporary credentials to the staff member; generate a replacement temporary password when needed.
Sign in with the temporary password and complete the required password change.
Review Assigned Documents; deactivate users or unused roles, or Remove an eligible unused role.

notes: Additional roles combine the permissions available to a user. The Leader is used by approval routes that name the requester's leader.
A delegated administrator cannot grant permissions they do not hold or create an Administrator role assignment.
Roles still used by accounts or approval routes cannot be removed. Account and role actions each require their own permission.

pages.title: Publish approval routes for future requests
pages.summary: A workflow administrator changes the ordered approval steps without changing routes already captured by requests.

steps.text: Open Workflow Builder and select the request type and its version.
Choose Start First Draft or Create Next Draft.
Choose Add Approval Step; name the step and select a role, person, requester's leader or requester.
Choose Save Step; edit, reorder or Remove steps until the route matches the business process.
Choose Validate & Publish and confirm.
Make the valid route the published default for future submissions; retain existing requests' captured routes.

notes: Published versions are read-only. Create a draft to change future approvals.
Submission must resolve active approvers. A route that needs a requester's leader cannot start without an active assigned leader.
The active published route determines who acts next; default approval examples are not a permanent company-wide rule.

pages.title: Follow reminders and review recorded actions
pages.summary: Staff use reminders to find work needing attention. An authorized auditor reviews the recorded system actions.

steps.text: Check the counts beside My Requests and My Tasks and open the relevant tab.
Highlight the staff member's Draft or Returned requests, assigned approvals and physical handoff tasks.
Open a task reminder and review the request before taking its permitted action.
When a retention reminder appears, open the hardcopy record and review the due or overdue date.
Open Internal Audit Trail; use Search and filters to locate the recorded actions.
Open View Details to check who acted, when the action occurred and the recorded outcome.

notes: Approval Process Timeline and request history explain request decisions. Internal Audit Trail records wider system actions.
Reminders do not approve, dispatch, accept or dispose of documents; the responsible person still confirms the action.
Counts and alerts reflect the signed-in account's allowed work. Dates and times use Asia/Manila.

pages.title: Create, download and import a backup
pages.summary: An authorized backup operator keeps protected recovery copies and manages older archive files.

steps.text: Open Backup & Restore and check that backup setup is ready.
Choose Backup now and confirm to create an encrypted recovery archive.
Create and list the completed archive; show its type, creation time and size.
Choose Download to keep an approved backup in a secure location.
To add an existing archive, choose Import backup, select Backup ZIP and confirm.
When appropriate, choose Clean up and confirm removal of eligible archives older than three months.

notes: A backup contains system records, application code and private files. Routine temporary files and existing backup archives are excluded.
The daily automatic backup is scheduled for 5:00 PM, Asia/Manila, and needs the server scheduler configured.
Import verifies and stores a backup; it does not restore live data. Clean up applies to eligible backup, audit and log archives.

pages.title: Restore system data from a backup
pages.summary: An authorized backup operator replaces live records and private files with a verified backup, then signs in again.

steps.text: Open Backup & Restore and choose Restore system data.
Choose Backup to restore; enter Your password and type RESTORE to confirm.
Choose Restore selected backup and confirm replacement of the live records and private files.
Check the archive and authorization, then create a recovery backup before changing live data.
Block normal use during restoration; restore records and private files, then sign the restoring operator out.
Sign in again and check the restored records, attachments and normal business actions.

notes: Plan a maintenance period: restoration replaces current records and private files with the selected backup's contents.
The restore screen uses the operator's account password. The server must also be configured to open and verify the protected archive.
The web restore does not replace application code. A system maintainer handles code recovery separately when needed.
